mouthText: Sundarbans Delta into Bay of Bengal (Meghna estuary)

waypoints.title: Stage 1: Glacial Source at Gaumukh
waypoints.description: Emerges as the Bhagirathi River from the snout of the Gangotri Glacier at Gaumukh (3,892 m) in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.
waypoints.examNote: Bhagirathi is considered the source stream of the Ganga in mythology and official geography.

waypoints.title: Stage 2: Tehri Dam (Tallest Dam in India)
waypoints.description: India's tallest dam (260.5 m rock and earth-fill embankment) impounding the Bhagirathi and Bhilangna rivers, generating 2,400 MW.
waypoints.examNote: Subject of Sundarlal Bahuguna's historic Chipko and anti-dam environmental resistance.

waypoints.title: Stage 3: Devprayag Confluence (Birth of Name 'Ganga')
waypoints.description: The turbulent Bhagirathi merges with the calm, voluminous Alaknanda at Devprayag. Downstream from this fifth and final Panch Prayag confluence, the combined river is officially named the Ganga.
waypoints.examNote: Panch Prayag sequence from north to south: Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga) -> Nandaprayag (Nandakini) -> Karnaprayag (Pindar) -> Rudraprayag (Mandakini) -> Devprayag (Bhagirathi + Alaknanda).

waypoints.title: Stage 4: Haridwar (Emergence into the Northern Plains)
waypoints.description: The Ganga breaks through the Siwalik foothills and enters the vast alluvial Indo-Gangetic Plains. Here the Upper Ganga Canal diverts water for agricultural irrigation across western UP.
waypoints.examNote: Hosted the historic 1854 Upper Ganga Canal built by British engineer Proby Cautley.

waypoints.title: Stage 5: Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam)
waypoints.description: Confluence of India's two greatest rivers: the Ganga and its largest right-bank tributary, the Yamuna (along with the mythical subterranean Saraswati).
waypoints.examNote: Site of the Maha Kumbh Mela (inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list).

waypoints.title: Stage 6: Varanasi (Kashi)
waypoints.description: The river takes a north-flowing crescent arc (Uttravahini Ganga) through one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited spiritual and educational capitals.
waypoints.examNote: National Waterway 1 (NW-1) multimodal cargo terminal operates here under the Jal Marg Vikas Project.

waypoints.title: Stage 7: Farakka Barrage Bifurcation
waypoints.description: A 2,240 m barrage in Murshidabad (West Bengal) where the Ganga bifurcates into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly (flowing south through West Bengal to Kolkata) and the main stream entering Bangladesh as the Padma.
waypoints.examNote: Subject of the 1996 Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty.

waypoints.title: Stage 8: Sundarbans Delta & Bay of Bengal
waypoints.description: The combined Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna discharges into the Bay of Bengal, forming the world's largest mangrove delta: the UNESCO World Heritage Sundarbans.
waypoints.examNote: Home of the Royal Bengal Tiger and the endangered Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica), India's National Aquatic Animal.

originText: Angsi Glacier (Mount Kailash vicinity, western Tibet - 5,300 m)
mouthText: Bay of Bengal (via Meghna confluence in Bangladesh)

waypoints.title: Stage 1: Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet
waypoints.description: Flows eastward parallel to the Great Himalayas for ~1,700 km as the high-altitude Yarlung Tsangpo through the arid Tibetan plateau.
waypoints.examNote: Known as the world's highest major river, flowing at an average elevation above 4,000 meters.

waypoints.title: Stage 2: The Great Bend around Namcha Barwa
waypoints.description: Carves the colossal Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon (deepest canyon on Earth) making a dramatic hairpin U-turn around the eastern Himalayan anchor peak Namcha Barwa (7,782 m).
waypoints.examNote: Classical antecedent drainage demonstrating that the river predates the uplift of the Himalayan mountains.

waypoints.title: Stage 3: Siang / Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh
waypoints.description: Enters India near Gelling in the Upper Siang district of Arunachal Pradesh as the roaring Siang River, descending through spectacular gorges.
waypoints.examNote: Site of strategic hydropower proposals and flood mitigation monitoring.

waypoints.title: Stage 4: Sadiya Tri-Confluence (Birth of Name 'Brahmaputra')
waypoints.description: Near Sadiya in Assam, the Dihang is joined by two massive left-bank tributaries: the Dibang and the Lohit. Downstream of this tri-junction, it assumes the name Brahmaputra.
waypoints.examNote: Connected by the 9.15 km Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola-Sadiya Bridge) across the Lohit River, India's longest bridge over water.

waypoints.title: Stage 5: Majuli Island (World's Largest River Island)
waypoints.description: Braided channels enclose Majuli, the world's largest inhabited river island and the cultural epicenter of Srimanta Sankardeva's Neo-Vaishnavite Satra culture.
waypoints.examNote: First island district in India, declared in 2016 by the Government of Assam.

waypoints.title: Stage 6: Kaziranga & Guwahati (Saraighat)
waypoints.description: Flows along Kaziranga National Park (One-Horned Rhinoceros habitat) and narrows at Guwahati where the historic Battle of Saraighat (1671) took place under Ahom general Lachit Borphukan.
waypoints.examNote: National Waterway 2 (NW-2) operates from Dhubri to Sadiya along the Brahmaputra.

waypoints.title: Stage 7: Enters Bangladesh as the Jamuna
waypoints.description: Loops around the Garo Hills near Dhubri and turns southward into Bangladesh, where it is known as the Jamuna River before joining the Padma (Ganga) at Goalundo.
waypoints.examNote: Its massive sediment yield is the second highest in the world after the Yellow River (Huang He).

mouthText: Bay of Bengal (Gautami & Vasishta mouths near Yanam)

waypoints.title: Stage 1: Source at Trimbakeshwar
waypoints.description: Originates from the Brahmagiri Mountain at Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra, site of one of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas.
waypoints.examNote: Second longest river in India and the longest Peninsular river system (accounting for nearly 10% of India's total geographic area).

waypoints.title: Stage 2: Jayakwadi Dam (Nath Sagar)
waypoints.description: Major earthen multipurpose dam in Paithan (Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), supplying water to the drought-prone Marathwada region.
waypoints.examNote: Jayakwadi Bird Sanctuary around Nath Sagar reservoir is home to numerous migratory avian species.

waypoints.title: Stage 3: Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project
waypoints.description: World's largest multi-stage lift irrigation project at the confluence of the Godavari and Pranhita rivers in Telangana.
waypoints.examNote: Pranhita (formed by confluence of Wardha, Penganga, and Wainganga) brings over 34% of Godavari's total water discharge.

waypoints.title: Stage 4: Polavaram Project & Papi Hills Gorge
waypoints.description: Pierces through the picturesque gorge of Papi Hills (Papi Kondalu) in the Eastern Ghats where the national multi-purpose Polavaram irrigation dam is built.
waypoints.examNote: Declared a National Irrigation Project under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act 2014.

waypoints.title: Stage 5: Rajahmundry & Deltaic Discharge
waypoints.description: Reaches the delta head at Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage (Dowleswaram Barrage) near Rajahmundry, bifurcating into two main distributaries: Gautami Godavari and Vasishta Godavari into the Bay of Bengal.
waypoints.examNote: Forms the fertile Krishna-Godavari (KG) delta basin, also celebrated for the offshore KG-D6 deep-water natural gas discoveries.

riverName: Narmada (Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat)
originText: Amarkantak Plateau (Maikal Range, Anuppur, MP - 1,057 m)
mouthText: Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea near Bharuch)

waypoints.title: Stage 1: Origin at Amarkantak
waypoints.description: Rises from Narmada Kund on the sacred Amarkantak plateau in the Maikal Range of eastern Madhya Pradesh.
waypoints.examNote: Radial drainage center where the Narmada flows west, the Son flows north-east to the Ganga, and the Johilla flows into Son.

waypoints.title: Stage 2: Dhuandhar Falls & Marble Rocks (Jabalpur)
waypoints.description: Plunges 30 meters at the Dhuandhar ('Smoky Cascades') waterfall and carves a spectacular 3 km gorge through gleaming white magnesium marble cliffs at Bhedaghat.
waypoints.examNote: Classic geological example of river incision through crystalline limestone / dolomite rocks.

waypoints.title: Stage 3: The Great Rift Valley Flow
waypoints.description: Flows westward through a tectonic fault trough (graben) between two block mountain ranges: the Vindhyas to the north and the Satpuras to the south.
waypoints.examNote: Because it flows in a rigid fault-guided rift valley, the Narmada and Tapi do not form deltas; they form clean estuaries!

waypoints.title: Stage 4: Indira Sagar Dam (Narmadanagar)
waypoints.description: India's largest reservoir by water storage capacity (12.22 billion cubic meters), located in the Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh.
waypoints.examNote: Mother project for downstream irrigation dams including Omkareshwar and Maheshwar.

waypoints.title: Stage 5: Sardar Sarovar Dam & Statue of Unity
waypoints.description: Major concrete gravity dam (138.68 m height) in Gujarat feeding the 458 km long Narmada Main Canal to arid Saurashtra and Kutch. Overlooked by the 182-meter Statue of Unity.
waypoints.examNote: Centerpiece of Medha Patkar's Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA) environmental movement.

waypoints.title: Stage 6: Estuary into the Gulf of Khambhat
waypoints.description: Forms a wide 25 km tidal estuary near Bharuch in Gujarat, draining cleanly into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).
waypoints.examNote: Longest west-flowing river of Peninsular India; produces no delta due to rapid tidal scouring.
